title: Transactional Commit Queue with Rollback Support
concept: Two-Phase Commit & Rollback on Host Mutation Failures
problemStatement: Implement `createTransactionalReconciler()` that stages host mutations in a queue. If any mutation in the batch throws during commit, all previously executed mutations in that batch MUST be rolled back to their previous state.
interviewTrap: During Concurrent Mode, if React aborts a render, work-in-progress fibers are simply discarded without touching the host DOM. But once the commit phase starts, mutations must either succeed cleanly or trigger an error boundary.

testCases.name: Commits staged mutations successfully
testCases.testFn: let a = 0; const r = createTransactionalReconciler(); r.stage({ execute: () => a += 1, rollback: () => a -= 1 }); const res = r.commit(); return res.success && a === 1;

testCases.name: Rolls back previously executed mutations if an error occurs mid-commit
testCases.input: first op modifies val, second op throws -> val restored
testCases.testFn: let state = 0; const r = createTransactionalReconciler(); r.stage({ execute: () => state = 10, rollback: () => state = 0 }); r.stage({ execute: () => { throw new Error('DOM Error'); }, rollback: () => {} }); r.commit(); return state;

testCases.name: Clears staged operations queue after execution
testCases.input: re-committing empty queue succeeds with no extra operations
testCases.testFn: const r = createTransactionalReconciler(); r.stage({ execute: () => {}, rollback: () => {} }); r.commit(); return r.commit().success;
